sources.description: OKX public REST market data for USDT-margined perpetual swaps (candles, trades, books, ticker, funding rates). No API key; read-only.

endpoints.expected_structure: JSON object with code "0" and a data list of 9-element rows [ts, open, high, low, close, volume, volCcy, volCcyQuote, confirm]
endpoints.used_for: Recent candlesticks (latest bars, forming bar included)

endpoints.expected_structure: Same row shape as /market/candles; rows strictly older than the after cursor, newest first, at most 100 per page
JSON object with code "0" and a data list of trade objects (tradeId, px, sz, side, ts)
endpoints.used_for: Historical trades, paged backwards by trade ID

endpoints.expected_structure: JSON object with code "0" and a data list with asks/bids arrays and a ts
JSON object with code "0" and a data list with fundingRate, nextFundingRate, fundingTime
endpoints.used_for: Live funding rate (mid-interval estimate) and next funding time

endpoints.expected_structure: JSON object with code "0" and a data list with fundingRate and fundingTime (settlement ms)

quirks.statement: Daily (1D) bars open at 16:00 UTC (midnight UTC+8); a bar becomes knowable at its close, 24 hours after its open.

quirks.recheck: Fetch one history-candles page with after=<now> and one with before=<now>; the before page is empty.
quirks.statement: history-candles pagination uses after=<ts> (bars strictly older, newest first); sending before returns empty data.

quirks.recheck: Bisect trade IDs from the live head until the oldest retrievable trade (see docs/microstructure.md).
quirks.statement: history-trades retention is about 90 calendar days: the oldest retrievable BTC-USDT-SWAP trade was 2843636428, dated 2026-08-20 00:01:56 UTC, found by bisection.

quirks.recheck: Page after=<ms> backwards from the live head until the oldest row.
quirks.statement: funding-rate-history retention is about 93 days (280 rows per instrument); the floor moves (a 281st row seen minutes before the fetch was gone by fetch time) and must be re-established on every pull.
funding-rate-history pagination uses after only; before acts as a lower bound and does not page.

quirks.recheck: Compare the live funding-rate value with the history row at the next settlement.
quirks.statement: The live funding-rate value read mid-interval is an estimate, not the settled rate for that interval (the 4b input 0.0000215 was an estimate; the settled rate was 0.00006348).
Funding settles on the 00:00/08:00/16:00 UTC grid; the funding-rate cap/floor is ±0.375% per interval.

quirks.recheck: Re-read the OKX fee notice page and compare the Regular tier.
quirks.statement: Fee schedule (Regular): maker 0.0200% / taker 0.0500% on notional, per the OKX fee-adjustment notice effective 2026-09-09.

sources.retention: Candles: full history served via history-candles (bounded by instrument listing). history-trades: ~90 days. funding-rate-history: ~93 days, moving floor. No publication lag: bars are knowable at their close.

sources.description: Deribit public REST API: option instrument listings and the Deribit Volatility Index (DVOL). No API key; read-only.

endpoints.expected_structure: JSON object with a result list of instrument objects (instrument_name, base_currency, kind, option_type, strike, expiration_timestamp ms)
endpoints.used_for: Listed and recently expired option contracts

endpoints.expected_structure: JSON object with result.data, a list of 5-element rows [timestamp_ms, open, high, low, close]

quirks.recheck: Fetch expired=true and count distinct expiry dates; the recorded behaviour is exactly one.
quirks.statement: get_instruments with expired=true returns only the most recent expired batch (70 contracts, expiry 2026-11-17 at probe time), not the full history of expired contracts; it cannot reconstruct a historical expiry calendar.
get_volatility_index_data requires a currency parameter; omitting it returns HTTP 400.

quirks.recheck: Fetch listed BTC/ETH instruments and compare their forward expiry sets.
quirks.statement: Monthly options expire on the last Friday of the month, 08:00 UTC; listed BTC and ETH contracts each show 11 identical forward expiries, all last Fridays (Deribit Contract Introduction Policy states the rule verbatim).
DVOL daily points are timestamped 00:00 UTC.

quirks.recheck: Re-fetch the full DVOL history per currency and recount the points and gaps.
quirks.statement: 2,065 DVOL points per currency, 2021-03-24 to 2026-11-17, no gaps.
Instrument listings carry base_currency (the underlying); the adapter parses the underlying from it.

quirks.recheck: Fetch one instrument listing and inspect the top-level keys of a returned contract.
quirks.statement: Instrument listings carry no top-level currency field.

sources.retention: Listed instruments: current listings only. Expired instruments: most recent batch only. DVOL: full history served (from 2021-03-24). No publication lag.

sources.description: FRED free fredgraph CSV: daily economic series (VIXCLS, VXNCLS, VXTYN, DGS10, BAA10Y, CPIAUCSL). No API key.

endpoints.expected_structure: CSV with header [observation_date, <SERIES>]; strictly increasing dates; missing values are empty fields
endpoints.used_for: One series as CSV (observation_date, value); cosd/coed bound the window

sources.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

quirks.statement: fredgraph CSV works without an API key; no licensed series is used.
Custom or browser-like User-Agent requests hang (bare Mozilla/5.0 and a full Chrome UA both timed out); send no User-Agent header and let urllib identify itself.
Missing values are empty fields, not "." (the adapter treats both as missing; market holidays carry an empty field).

quirks.recheck: Fetch VIXCLS/DGS10 before the morning posting and compare the last date with the previous trading day (see study 007).
quirks.statement: Publication lag is one trading day (N=1): a value dated t is posted on the next business day. Verified behaviourally at 2026-11-18 06:26 UTC (01:26 EST): VIXCLS and DGS10 both ended at 2026-11-16, ruling out same-evening posting and a two-day lag.
FRED series VXTYN is the TYVIX history; the series is discontinued and still ends 2020-05-15.

quirks.recheck: Fetch the full VXTYN series and check the first date and row count.
quirks.statement: VXTYN covers 2003-01-02 to 2020-05-15 (4,363 rows in the study-003 manifest).

quirks.recheck: Search the FRED catalogue for a TYVIX or MOVE series.
quirks.statement: FRED has no TYVIX series and no MOVE series.
VXTYN has a genuine two-day gap on 2004-11-10 and 2004-11-11 (verified against a fresh pull; DGS10 has a value those days).
Licensed series are truncated on FRED; the lab used BAA10Y as the credit spread instead of a licensed spread series.
Series are current vintage and are revised over time; as-released values would need ALFRED or an API key.

sources.retention: Full history served per series (current vintage). Publication lag: one trading day (study 007, N=1). VXTYN discontinued 2020-05-15.

sources.description: Yahoo Finance public chart endpoint: daily bars for ^GSPC (S&P 500) as the equity factor. No API key.

endpoints.expected_structure: JSON with chart.result[0]: meta (symbol, longName), timestamp list, indicators.quote[0].close list of the same length
endpoints.used_for: Daily bars (timestamps, closes) for one symbol

quirks.recheck: Fetch the chart without a User-Agent and confirm Yahoo returns 401/403.
quirks.statement: The chart endpoint requires a browser-like User-Agent (Mozilla/5.0); without one Yahoo returns 401/403.

quirks.recheck: Fetch the ^MOVE chart and read meta.longName.
quirks.statement: Yahoo ^MOVE is a Northern Trust iBoxx ETF, not the ICE BofA MOVE index — always check meta.longName before trusting a ticker.

quirks.recheck: Fetch the ^TYVIX chart; the error payload confirms the delisting.
quirks.statement: Yahoo ^TYVIX is delisted ("No data found, symbol may be delisted").

quirks.recheck: Fetch a recent window and confirm the bar timestamps are the 09:30 ET market open (14:30 UTC in winter, 13:30 in summer) and that null closes are counted as missing.
quirks.statement: Bar timestamps are the market open (09:30 ET); closes use the 21:00 UTC convention shared with FRED; null closes are missing days and are excluded and counted.

sources.retention: Full history served per symbol. No publication lag: the close is knowable at the close.

sources.description: Treasury auction calendar: the Fiscal Data API auctions_query dataset, cross-checked against the TreasuryDirect auctioned endpoint. No API key. Descriptive use only (study 006).

endpoints.expected_structure: JSON with a data list of records (auction_date, security_type, ...) and meta.total-count
endpoints.used_for: Auction records (bills, notes, bonds) in a date window

endpoints.expected_structure: JSON list of auctioned securities with auction dates
endpoints.used_for: Cross-check: the 250 most recent auctioned securities

sources.provider: U.S. Treasury, Fiscal Data API (with TreasuryDirect as cross-check)

quirks.recheck: Fetch the most recent auctions and compare the latest auction date with the TreasuryDirect listing.
quirks.statement: The Fiscal Data API lags the live auction schedule by about four weeks (its coverage ended 2026-10-22 at study-006 fetch time); each probe re-observes the latest auction date and reports the current lag.

quirks.recheck: Re-fetch both endpoints and recompute the overlap.
quirks.statement: TreasuryDirect cross-check on the overlap window (2025-05-27 to 2026-10-22): 134 coupon dates on each side, symmetric difference empty.
The 7 most recent coupon dates (2026-10-26 to 2026-11-12) come from the TreasuryDirect tail supplement, flagged as such in the calendar file.
Coupon auction closings are 01:00 PM ET (536 records) or 11:30 AM ET (92 records); the 11:30 minority's results sit near the 16:00 UTC bar boundary.

sources.retention: Full history served per dataset. Publication lag: about four weeks behind the live auction schedule (study 006).

sources.description: FOMC meeting calendar pages: per-year historical pages (2003–2020) and the calendar page (2021 onwards). Public schedule data, no key.

endpoints.expected_structure: HTML page with one <h5> heading per meeting (date range and type)
HTML page with year sections listing scheduled meetings
endpoints.used_for: Current and future meeting calendar, 2021 onwards (year sections)

sources.provider: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

quirks.recheck: Re-fetch the calendar page and re-run the study-005 calendar checks (8/year, 7 in 2020).
quirks.statement: The calendar was extracted from fomchistorical{YYYY}.htm (2003–2020) and fomccalendars.htm (2021 onwards): 199 scheduled meetings 2003–2027, 8 per year (7 in 2020).
Statements are released around 14:00 ET on the last meeting day; t=0 is the statement day and the daily close already contains the reaction.
31 meetings are excluded from the scheduled set: 20 conference calls, 5 unscheduled meetings, 1 cancelled meeting (2020-03-17–18), 5 notation votes.

sources.retention: Historical pages are stable documents; the calendar page is updated as meetings are scheduled. No publication lag for past meetings.

sources.auth: none — public pages, no key (but programmatic access is blocked)
sources.description: BLS Schedule of Selected Releases annual pages (CPI release dates). Manual-only: BLS blocks programmatic requests.

endpoints.used_for: CPI release dates for the year

sources.manual_check: Open the BLS Schedule of Selected Releases page (https://www.bls.gov/schedule/) in a browser, read the CPI release dates for the current year, and compare them with research/macro-windows-006/cpi_calendar.json. Do not curl the page: BLS returns HTTP 403 to programmatic requests.

quirks.recheck: Open the BLS schedule page in a browser and compare the CPI release dates with research/macro-windows-006/cpi_calendar.json.
quirks.statement: BLS returns HTTP 403 to direct programmatic requests, including with a browser user-agent; the CPI calendar is a text-fetch transcription, not structured BLS API output.

quirks.recheck: Re-transcribe one full year from the BLS archive page and compare.
quirks.statement: The CPI calendar (71 releases, 2021-01-13 to 2026-12-10) was transcribed from the BLS archived schedule pages and cross-checked against the BLS archive page and two independent public lists.

quirks.recheck: Check the BLS shutdown FAQ and the archived CPI news releases page.
quirks.statement: The October 2025 CPI was never published (2025 federal shutdown); the September 2025 CPI was delayed to 2025-10-24.

sources.retention: Schedule pages are published annually in advance; release dates occasionally shift (shutdowns). Manual transcription only.
